activities.anchor: Look at Earth from space and two places demand
activities.caption: drag the divider — pole vs equator
activities.name: ebPolesCompare

config.prompt: Same planet, same Sun — drag the divider:

before.label: The South Pole
before.text: A sheet of ice so white and vast it reads as cloud — no green, no grey, almost nothing moving.

after.label: The equator
after.text: A band of green so dense it looks painted on — more tree species in a single hectare than all of Europe holds.

config.why: A few thousand kilometres apart — the rest of the lesson is the chain of ideas that explains the difference: ecosystems, biomes, and the syllabus's deliberately paired case studies.

activities.caption: file each part: biotic or abiotic
activities.name: ebPondSort

config.prompt: Every ecosystem runs on both — file each part:

items.label: fish, pondweed, insects, a visiting heron
fungi and bacteria breaking down dead material

config.why: An ecosystem is both together — all the organisms in an area plus the physical conditions they live in, linked by energy flow and nutrient cycling; the pond works only because the flows work.

activities.anchor: the whole system would smother in its own litter
activities.caption: line up the chain, base to return
activities.name: ebChainOrder

config.prompt: From captured sunlight back around again — sequence the chain:
items: producers (plants on land, algae at sea) capture sunlight
many food chains weave into a food web
decomposers — fungi and bacteria — break down dead material, releasing nutrients
the nutrients are used again by the producers
config.why: Food chains line the steps up — grass, rabbit, fox — but the web is the more honest picture; beneath everything runs the quieter recycling web that keeps the matter cycle from jamming.

activities.caption: true or false — what recycles, what leaks
activities.name: ebRecycleJudge

statements.s: Energy in a food chain is recycled, just like matter.
statements.why: The recycling applies to matter only — energy mostly leaves the living system as heat and is gone for good.

statements.s: When a fox catches a rabbit, the rabbit becomes fox, waste and warmth.
statements.why: That is matter's journey — the same atoms served a billion meals before.

statements.s: Heat that leaks from one feeding step returns to power the next.
statements.why: It never comes back — which is why energy must keep arriving.

statements.s: The Sun never stops paying in, while the same water and carbon atoms have served a billion meals.
statements.why: One-way energy, cycling matter — the two flows behave differently, and the difference matters.

activities.anchor: Even at midsummer the Sun barely lifts above the horizon
activities.caption: pin Vostok's annual mean
activities.name: ebVostokPlace

config.prompt: Vostok station's annual mean sits at what temperature?
config.why: About −55 °C — and the lowest surface temperature ever recorded on Earth, −89.2 °C, was measured there on 21 July 1983. Cold, dense air pools over the continent as high pressure, and domes make deserts: under 50 mm of water equivalent a year in the interior.

activities.anchor: Air spilling off the Antarctic high
activities.caption: call the windiest place's average
activities.name: ebWindEstimate

config.prompt: Cape Denison is the windiest place at sea level on Earth. Its annual average wind speed is about —?
config.why: 70–80 km/h — cold, dense air pouring off an ice dome the way water pours off a roof, where Douglas Mawson's expedition wintered in 1912. At the equator the story inverts into the steady trade winds, deflected sideways by Earth's rotation.

activities.anchor: carry a mechanism's worth of adaptation
activities.caption: pair each specialist with its trick
activities.name: ebAdaptMatch

config.prompt: The Southern Ocean's specialists — pair each with its adaptation:

pairs.right: the male incubates the single egg on his feet through roughly four months of darkness, fasting throughout
no red pigment at all — cold water holds enough dissolved oxygen — plus glycoprotein antifreeze that binds invading ice crystals
keep their breathing holes open by grinding them with their teeth
can shrink, moulting down through foodless winters — a trick almost unique to them

config.why: The web has a calendar, and the calendar is the sea ice: each austral spring, melting ice and returning light trigger blooms so dense the ice underside turns brown, and krill larvae need that underside as nursery and cafeteria through winter.

activities.caption: true or false — the threats, with their numbers
activities.name: ebThreatJudge

statements.s: The krill fishery takes up to about 450,000 tonnes a year, against a precautionary trigger limit of 620,000.
statements.why: A thin margin by design — the trigger exists explicitly to leave enough for penguins and seals.

statements.s: The Antarctic Peninsula warmed by close to 3 °C over the late twentieth century.
statements.why: Among the fastest-warming places on Earth.

statements.s: The whole ice sheet is losing around 150 billion tonnes a year.
statements.why: Satellite measurements reckon it so — a number with sea-level stakes attached.

statements.s: Tourism has collapsed to under 10,000 visitors a season.
statements.why: The opposite — just over 100,000 visitors in 2022–23, concentrated at a handful of landing sites in a few summer weeks.
